skill.name: competitor-alternatives
skill.description: Guides the creation of SEO-focused competitor alternative and comparison pages. It covers page formats, research inputs, modular competitor data, section templates, and maintenance practices.
skill.summary: Create fair competitor alternative pages, comparison pages, and supporting SEO content.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.value_statement: Competitive search pages often become shallow feature tables that buyers do not trust. This skill helps create fair, research-backed alternative and comparison pages for SEO and sales enablement.
actual_capabilities: Defines four competitor page formats: singular alternative, plural alternatives, direct comparison, and competitor-versus-competitor pages.
Provides recommended page structures, URL patterns, keyword targets, and tone guidance for each format.
Shows how to centralize competitor data so pricing, strengths, weaknesses, and migration notes stay consistent.
Includes reusable section templates for summaries, feature comparisons, pricing, support, audience fit, migration, and social proof.
Adds guidance for index pages, internal linking, FAQ schema, research sources, and refresh cadence.
limitations: It does not verify live competitor pricing, features, or search volume automatically.
It needs accurate product positioning, competitor names, customer quotes, and migration details from the user.
It does not create CMS templates, publish pages, or manage deployment workflows.
Competitive claims may need legal, brand, or compliance review before publication.

use_cases.title: Build a competitor alternative page
use_cases.description: Create a page for buyers searching for an alternative to a named competitor, with honest positioning and migration guidance.

use_cases.title: Plan a comparison content hub
use_cases.description: Map index pages, internal links, URL patterns, and priority competitor topics for a scalable comparison content program.

use_cases.title: Support competitive sales conversations
use_cases.description: Turn competitor research into fair comparison copy that sales teams can use during buyer evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a simple alternative page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one competitor and basic positioning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an outline for a [Competitor] alternative page for [Product]. Our main differentiator is [Differentiator], and our ideal customer is [Audience].

prompt_templates.title: Write a fair comparison page
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a direct product comparison.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [Product] vs [Competitor] page plan. Include a TL;DR, comparison sections, who each product fits, migration notes, and CTA ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Create a comparison hub plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple competitor pages and internal linking.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a competitor comparison content plan for [Product]. Use these competitors: [List]. Include page types, URL patterns, hub pages, internal links, and priority order.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh existing competitor content
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced maintenance request for accuracy and trust.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this competitor page draft for accuracy, fairness, buyer usefulness, SEO coverage, and missing proof. Suggest specific updates and sections to add.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a Notion alternative page outline for a project management product.
output: A recommended URL and target keyword set.
A section-by-section page outline with buyer intent notes.
Guidance on where to include proof, migration details, and honest competitor strengths.

output_examples.input: An SEO lead asks for a comparison hub covering five competitors.
output: A prioritized list of alternative and comparison pages.
Index page recommendations for alternatives and versus pages.
Internal linking guidance that connects hub pages, feature pages, and individual comparisons.

output_examples.input: A product marketer asks how to make a pricing comparison more credible.
output: A pricing section structure that covers tiers, included features, add-ons, and total cost.
Suggestions for adding caveats, source dates, and buyer-fit guidance.
Warnings against unsupported claims or outdated competitor details.

best_practices: Use current competitor research, customer proof, and clear source dates for claims that buyers can verify.
Acknowledge competitor strengths and your own tradeoffs so the comparison feels credible.
Centralize competitor data and refresh pricing, features, and positioning on a regular schedule.
anti_patterns: Do not publish generic feature checklists without explaining why differences matter.
Do not exaggerate competitor weaknesses or hide cases where the competitor is a better fit.
Do not reuse stale pricing, reviews, or product details across pages without verification.

faq.question: What types of pages does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It supports alternative pages, alternatives roundup pages, direct product comparisons, competitor-versus-competitor pages, and index pages.

faq.question: Does it perform competitor research automatically?
faq.answer: No. It gives a research process and content structure, but users must supply or verify current competitor information.

faq.question: Can it help with SEO planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes keyword patterns, URL structures, index page guidance, internal linking, and FAQ schema suggestions.

faq.question: Is it only for SaaS products?
faq.answer: No. The framework is strongest for software, but it can adapt to other products with clear competitors and buyer criteria.

faq.question: How should teams keep comparison pages accurate?
faq.answer: They should centralize competitor data, verify pricing and features quarterly, and update pages when major competitor changes appear.

faq.question: Can this replace legal or brand review?
faq.answer: No. Teams should review competitive claims, customer quotes, and pricing comparisons before publication.
